requirement:
The generated coverage subchapter MUST make coverage-collection and
post-suite-checking guidance available under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.guidance`, without requiring
separate authored content.
rationale:
The subject requires the generated coverage subchapter to carry coverage-collection and post-suite-checking guidance, as described by `requirements.test-coverage.check.guidance`, without authored content.

`src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` is marked {test} for this requirement. It builds the book through `fixture()`, whose only coverage chapter holds an empty `:::{coverage-index}` directive and no authored guidance. It then runs `populate_in` over two section-number variants, numbered and unnumbered.

On the generated `coverage` chapter it asserts that:
- The text contains `habeas test`, `habeas coverage -- --workspace` and `habeas coverage-check`.
- The text says to run `habeas coverage-check` "as a separate step" after the instrumented run succeeds.
- The text says `habeas test` collects coverage for the whole workspace and then checks it.
- The text says the static validation test needs no prior coverage.
- The text covers the rest of the setup guidance, including the 80% target and the `habeas:coverage` marker.
- The directive text `:::{coverage-index}` is gone from the generated output.

These assertions cover the obligation that this subchapter makes the guidance available, and the authored-content-free fixture covers "without requiring separate authored content".

The remaining obligations belong to `requirements.test-coverage.check.guidance`: the bundled agent instructions, the setup-generated docs, and the static validation test's behavior. That requirement is cited as context and carries its own tests, so I did not assess them here.

I found no gap.
